name: Gibson House Museum
description: A Back Bay row house between Arlington and Berkeley Streets, now a private nonprofit house museum. Its four floors of period rooms, including the original kitchen, preserve domestic life with original wallpapers, carpets, furniture, and family heirlooms. Working spaces such as the kitchen, laundry room, and coal shed also remain.
significance_text: It was one of the first houses built in the Back Bay. Beginning in 1936, Charles Gibson Jr. decided to preserve the townhouse as a monument to his family's legacy, and it opened to the public as a museum in 1957. It is a National Historic Landmark and a City of Boston Registered Landmark.

admission.notes: Open year-round by guided tour only. Adults $15, seniors (62+) $12, students $10, children ages 6-12 $5. Tours last 45 minutes and move through four floors. Tours are not suitable for children ages 5 and under. There is no elevator or air conditioning. Walk-ins are welcome, but space is limited and advance purchase is recommended.
